scenario_description:
Objective: Keep Monday’s stair-heavy passenger-service extra from becoming a foot-comfort risk because the preventive heel-pad kit is empty.
Emerging Need: A short tentative station item grows into a long shift with repeated stair transfers, while the red kit lacks usable pads and a narrow station-hold option remains.
Decision Context: Saved podiatry guidance identifies when hydrocolloid heel pads matter, rules out casual substitutes, and defines the ordinary purchase limit; current funds and counter timing determine feasibility.
Consequence: If the counter window passes, the shift can proceed but may begin without the planned foot-protection supply.

parameter.title: Tentative station assist block
parameter.description: Reserve-board placeholder for a short indoor concourse assistance block if needed.

parameter.subject: Morning counter holds for travel-health shelf
parameter.body: For June 8 morning pickups, sealed hydrocolloid heel-pad six-packs are $9.50. Requests received before 08:30 can be held at the south concourse counter for pickup from 09:00 to 10:00; later requests roll to afternoon pickup.

parameter.title: Passenger-service extra 301: south stair transfers
parameter.description: Confirmed long extra with extended standing and three south-stair platform transfers during boarding assistance.

parameter.content: While sorting the entry table, I checked the red travel heel-pad kit by your rail bag. The sleeve inside is empty, and I put the empty kit back there. I’m out early tomorrow, so I won’t be able to check again after 07:00.

parameter.description: Cash loaded to personal travel wallet before the Union Station report.

parameter.subject: June 8 morning holds closed
parameter.body: Morning travel-health shelf holds closed at 08:30. New heel-pad pickup requests are now available after 11:15 only because the south counter is moving to midday inventory.
